transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, yeah, thanks. So, what made me come in is that for the past year or so, the smallest thing just completely derails me. Like, a phone buzz, somebody walking past my office, or even a random thought about my in-laws—which, by the way, my mother-in-law just bought this massive RV. She doesn't even like driving! I don't know why she thinks she's going to take a 40-foot motorhome across the country when she can barely parallel park her sedan. We went over there last weekend and it's just taking up the whole driveway. But anyway, yeah, a random thought like that just pulls me off what I’m doing before I can stop it. It's just... I can't seem to stay on track.
Do you ever have thoughts that come into your mind that you don’t want or that bother you, like they don’t fit with who you are?

No, not really. I mean, my thoughts are definitely mine, they don't bother me like that or feel weird. It's more just... there are a lot of them, you know? Like I’ll be looking at the quarterly projections for my company, and suddenly I’m wondering if the guys fixed the loading dock door at the warehouse. 

Which, by the way, we had to get a whole new track for it last week because one of the new forklift drivers backed straight into it. Just smashed the aluminum to pieces. And the kid tried to tell me the brakes slipped! I'm looking right at the skid marks on the concrete, and I know exactly what happened because I used to drive those exact same lifts before I started the business. I mean, I didn't even finish high school and I know how a brake pedal works, you know? I had to have my operations manager deal with the kid because I just didn't have the patience to listen to the excuses. 

But, uh... wait, what did you ask me? Something about thoughts? Yeah, no, nothing creepy or anything that doesn't feel like me. Just regular stuff, just... a lot of it jumping around.
Have you been feeling down, losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or feeling unusually tired or drained most days?

No, not really. I'm not down or depressed or anything. And I definitely haven't lost interest in my stuff. I still have plenty of energy for my hobbies. Actually, I just picked up a '69 Chevelle project car a couple weeks ago. The guy I bought it from kept it under a tarp in his backyard for, like, fifteen years. Can you believe that? Just letting a classic piece of Detroit steel rot in the mud. 

He said he was going to restore it with his son, but the kid ended up moving to Florida to do real estate. Which, honestly, the Florida real estate market right now is a complete mess. I was looking at some commercial properties down near Tampa for a second distribution center for my business, and the prices are just absolutely out of control. You can't even get a decent price per square foot unless you're way inland, and then you're paying a fortune in extra fuel and freight costs just to get the trucks back to the interstate. It makes zero business sense. I told my broker to just scrap the whole Florida idea and look at Georgia instead, because... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Being tired? Yeah, no, my energy is fine.
Do you often feel restless, have trouble staying focused, or find it hard to organize tasks and get things done?

Yeah, restless is a good word for it. It's like... when I'm supposed to just sit still, you know? Like at family dinners or those volunteer meetings my wife drags me to at the church. It literally feels like there's a motor running inside me and I just have to move or do something with my hands. 

Actually, at the last church meeting, they were talking about the annual bake sale, which is fine, but they spent forty-five minutes arguing about whether to use paper plates or those little cardboard bakery boxes. I mean, forty-five minutes! I was tapping my foot so hard I think the lady next to me thought I was having a seizure. I ended up taking apart my pen and putting it back together about ten times. 

And speaking of pens, I just ordered these custom ones for the business. Really nice, heavy metal barrels with our logo laser-engraved. I got tired of those cheap plastic ones that break in half if you look at them wrong. The guy at the promotional company tried to upcharge me for blue ink, which is ridiculous. I told him, look, I'm buying five thousand units, you can throw in the blue ink for free or I'm taking my business to the guys across town. He caved immediately, obviously. You gotta know how to negotiate with these guys, they'll nickel and dime you to death if you let them. 

But, uh... wait. Did you ask about organizing tasks too? Because yeah, sitting still is tough. I just... I gotta be doing something.
Do you often act quickly without thinking things through, like interrupting others, making impulsive decisions, or feeling like you can't wait your turn?

Yeah, I do that a lot, actually. The interrupting thing. It's like I already know what they're gonna say, so I just say it for them to keep things moving. I do it with my employees all the time—I'll just finish their sentence before they can get it out. And I know it annoys them, I can see it on their faces. I do it to my wife, too, especially when she's on the phone with her parents. I'll just jump right in the middle of their conversation. 

Her parents, by the way, they just bought this massive RV. Like, one of those Class A motorhomes that costs as much as a house. They're planning to drive it up to Alaska next summer, which I think is completely insane. Have you seen the price of diesel lately? It's hovering around four bucks a gallon, and that thing probably gets, what, eight miles to the gallon on a good day? Plus, driving a rig that size on those mountain roads up in the Yukon... I told my father-in-law he's gonna burn out his transmission before he even crosses the Canadian border. I actually had to replace the transmission in one of our delivery box trucks last month because the driver kept riding the brakes down this steep grade on his route. Cost me four grand. I told the operations manager to fire the guy, but... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, acting without thinking. Yeah, the interrupting thing is definitely a problem. I just... I get impatient waiting for people to get to the point.
Do these issues with restlessness, staying focused, and acting quickly happen in different parts of your life, like at work, at home, and in social situations, or are they mostly limited to one area?

Yeah, it's pretty much everywhere. Work, home, out with friends... it doesn't really matter where I am. I mean, I'm still keeping up overall, running the business and everything, but it's starting to cause some friction. Like, I can tell it's costing me some trust at home with my wife, especially when we're trying to make family plans or I just talk over her. And at work, I'm definitely wearing down my team's patience. When we have meetings or I'm trying to mentor one of the younger guys, things just don't go the way they should because I can't sit still or I keep interrupting them. 

Speaking of the younger guys, I just hired this kid right out of high school to help out in the warehouse. Reminds me a lot of myself, actually. I dropped out in the 11th grade, you know? Just couldn't do the whole sitting at a desk thing all day. Best decision I ever made, honestly, because I started my first business a year later. Anyway, this kid, he's a hard worker, but he keeps showing up in these ridiculous, expensive sneakers. Like, the kind that cost four hundred bucks on the resale market. I told him, "Listen, man, you're moving pallets of auto parts, you're gonna ruin those shoes in a week." And sure enough, he dropped a box of brake rotors on his foot on Tuesday. Luckily he didn't break anything, but the shoe was completely trashed. I had to send him to the boot truck that comes by the industrial park every Wednesday to buy a proper pair of steel-toes. Which, by the way, the guy running that boot truck is making a killing. He's got zero overhead, just drives from lot to lot... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, the restlessness and stuff. It happens everywhere, pretty much. Work, home, you name it.
